title: fix(sse): handle partial JSON and delimiter ordering in SSE streaming framing
author: Avery Chen
release_notes: Fixes streaming SSE framing bugs that could produce malformed partial-JSON events and reorder delimiter tokens. Improves stability for OpenAI-compat streaming responses and reduces parsing errors for downstream SDKs.
description: Context: some customers and internal tests surfaced intermittent failures where streaming SSE responses would yield truncated or invalid partial JSON objects when the runtime emitted token/byte boundaries that interacted poorly with our framing code. Root causes: (1) delimiter bytes occasionally duplicated or emitted out-of-order when buffering logic and the final chunk flush interacted, and (2) the OpenAI-compatible response adapter wrapped events too eagerly, causing downstream consumers to receive incomplete JSON objects. This PR: - Reworks the SSE framer to explicitly track JSON token boundaries and only emit an 'event' line when the framer detects an end-of-object or when a configured safe byte threshold is reached. - Ensures delimiter insertion happens after atomic flushes to prevent duplicate or swapped delimiters when multiple internal buffers are drained in the same write path. - Adds a small per-stream reorder guard: events are stamped with a monotonic sequence id and reordered safely before delivery if necessary. This avoids transient reordering during concurrent buffer flushes. - Updates the OpenAI compatibility layer adapter to buffer partial text chunks and only forward structured JSON events once the framer signals completion. This avoids delivering partial JSON objects to SDKs implementing streaming partial JSON parsing. - Adds deterministic unit and fuzz tests that replicate known failure modes (split-token across SSE boundaries, duplicate delimiter injection, and rapid interleaved flushes). - Adds metrics for partial-json-emitted and framer-reorders to help detect regressions in production. Checklist: - [x] Implement framer fixes and reorder guard - [x] Update openai_compat adapter buffering - [x] Add unit + fuzz tests and fixtures - [x] Add docs note and migration guidance - [x] Run CI and fix flakes - [x] Add release notes and changelog entry Related: ENG-4821 (streaming stability), ENG-4890 (openai-compat incomplete json incidents).

discussion:
Jordan Lee: The framing approach looks cleaner than before; two questions: 1) the per-stream sequence id — do we have any pathological cases with wraparound on long lived streams? 2) how does this impact latency for large single-object responses?
Author (Avery Chen): Sequence id is a 64-bit monotonic counter per process; wraparound is astronomically unlikely and we add a safe-compare function to handle eventual wrap correctness. Latency: we add a configurable safe byte threshold (default 64KB) and a max-wait 25ms timer; for large single-object responses we will still stream data incrementally as soon as framer sees object boundaries or the threshold/timer fires — measured p50 increase <0.5ms in our perf lab.
Samir Patel: CI failed initially on test_sse_framing because the fixture ordering introduced nondeterminism. Thanks for the fix to the test harness. Please add a short comment in docs for operators who may tune the threshold.
Author: Added docs note with recommended threshold ranges and a description of the new "partial-json-emitted" metric.
Riley Morgan: Approving after seeing the fuzz harness and metrics added. Observability will help us detect regressions in production.
Merger (auto): squash and merge via UI after all approvals and CI green.

notes_for_release: Stability fixes for SSE streaming framing and OpenAI-compat adapter. This reduces malformed streaming JSON errors for users consuming partial JSON via the streaming endpoints. Operators can tune STREAM_FRAMER_SAFE_BYTES and STREAM_FRAMER_MAX_WAIT_MS if they have unusual tokenization patterns.
affected_sdks_notice: redwood-sdk-python and redwood-sdk-typescript: no API surface change, but consumers that parse streaming partial-JSON will see fewer parsing errors. Recommend updating to latest SDKs that include minor streaming parser resilience patches.
